title: refactor(sim): a field column's floor reads exactly from the shell, or is refused
body:
## What changed

**Stacked on #646** (#637 step A). Merge #646 first. This is **#637 step B**, option 2 from the design comment on #637.

**New `SdfField::floor_at(x, y) -> FloorRead`** (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/field_floor.rs`) reads the **lowest face of the stock under a column**.
- **How:** straight from the shell's own lowest crossing on that column. That's a mesh plane, so it's **exact**.
- **Why:** it's the column body's commonest re-clamp, a part flipped onto a face an earlier setup left uncut.
- **What it refuses:** a column whose floor a cut actually removed (a claim > 0 at or next to the floor cell) gets **`FloorRead::CutFromBelow`**, by name. The down-march's exactness rests on `cut_ups`, and no upward companion exists yet, so no bracketed guess is given. A `cut_downs` companion (option 1) can lift this later.
- **Other results:** `NoMaterial` for a column beside the stock, `Unreadable` for an `Open` parity column.
- **Not yet wired:** nothing uses it yet. It's for steps C–D.

**Also folded in, from the review of #646:** the `unapply` doc now says the round trip is exact **to rounding** (exactly for integer shifts, within an ulp of a fractional one), not "bit for bit".

## How tested

- **New `crates/sim/tests/field_floor.rs`, 2/2:**
  - `an_uncut_floor_reads_the_shell_exactly`: a plate's floor is −6.0 exactly. A shallow top slot leaves it −6.0, since a band reaching down isn't a cut floor. Beside the stock reads `NoMaterial`.
  - `a_floor_a_cut_reached_is_refused_by_name`: a slot cut through the plate gives `CutFromBelow` over the slot, and the floor beside it is still exactly −6.0.
- **`scripts/gate.sh quick`:** the sim suites pass. Named: field_carry 3, stock_backend_parity 13, stock_columns 3, and app setup_carry 9, carried_verify 8.
- **Clippy** on sim and app with `-D warnings`: clean. No golden changed.

## Not exercised

Steps C–E (the clip intersection, the body enum with its agreement lane, and the app holders), per #637.

Changelog: none (internal: a field floor read, not yet used)

Refs #637
Refs #26

title: fix(turning): facing approaches at rapid and lifts off the face before retracting
body:
**Stacked on #640** (#630, control-point posting, which changes the facing output). Review only this PR's own commit, `39ceb9c2`. The merge `c18542f9` brings in #640's latest tip.

**P2 (#632):** lathe facing had two problems.
1. Its first move after the tool call was a **feed** from wherever the turret was parked.
2. Every pass rapided straight out in X at the Z just cut, **dragging the nose across the fresh face**.

## What changed (`crates/motion/src/turning/face.rs`)
- **Approach:** the path starts on the axis at the clearance plane, the mill kernels' convention. Its first move is a **rapid to the clearance point (rho_clear, clearance)**, then the existing plunge feed.
  - Posted, the first motion after the tool call is `G00 X13 Z25`.
  - The meridian rapid law (#103) judges this rapid. rho_clear sits outside the stock radius, and a clearance plane inside the bar is refused (`RapidInStock`) and not posted.
- **Retract:** every pass lifts **`LIFT` = 0.2 mm (capped at half the stepdown)** up the axis, then rapids out in X at the lifted Z.
  - The cap keeps the lift inside air the pass above already cleared.
- **Profile Rough:** checked and unchanged. It already starts with a G0, and each rung exits radially outward at the top of its window, away from the finished diameter. This is recorded in the decision file.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/632-facing-approach.md`.

## Golden diff (`fanuc-lathe/facing.nc`)
- `G00 X13 Z25` is added before the first plunge.
- Each retract `G00 X13 Z<s>` becomes `G00 X-1.6 Z<s+0.2>` then `G00 X13 Z<s+0.2>`.
- The header's existing envelope-warning move index shifts by one. That fixture faces the part's own end by design, the same as on main.

## How tested
- **motion `turning_face`:**
  - `the_first_move_is_a_rapid_to_the_clearance_point`;
  - `every_pass_lifts_off_its_face_before_it_rapids_out` (3 stepdown/nose combinations, and no rapid slides along a cut face);
  - the stock-allowance test's rapid assertion is updated for the lift.
- **New app `turning_face_approach`:**
  - `the_first_posted_move_is_a_rapid_to_the_clearance_point`;
  - `every_facing_retract_lifts_z_before_it_moves_out_in_x`;
  - `a_clearance_plane_inside_the_bar_is_convicted_not_posted`.
- **Every new test fails on the old `face.rs`.**
- **Gate:**
  - camcraft-motion: 658 passed.
  - app, 31 binaries and 277 tests: conformance, golden_cl, posting, every lathe_* suite, every non-thread turning_* suite, drill_prior* and project_roundtrip.
  - Clippy is clean.
  - After merging #640's tip: lathe_stroke 7, lathe_post 7 and turning_face_approach 3 pass.

Changelog: Lathe facing now rapids to the clearance point before its first plunge and lifts 0.2 mm off each faced pass before retracting, instead of feeding in from the parked turret and dragging the nose across the fresh face (#632)

Fixes #632

title: refactor(sim): a field carried between setups is the same field seen through the turn
body:
## What changed

**#637 step A** (M7.3, the carried stock on the field engine). The design is in https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/637 (research comment).

- **New `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/field_carry.rs`:** `CarriedField` views an `SdfField` through a setup change's `LatticeTurn`. `distance(p) = field.distance(T⁻¹ p)`, and the same holds for `mesh_distance` and `inside`.
  - **Why it's exact:** a signed distance is **invariant under rigid motion**, so nothing is re-sampled. That's the field analogue of `carry`'s "re-index, never re-sample".
  - **Scope:** phase 1 stays on carry's eight lattice turns (Z kept on ±Z). Every other turn is still refused upstream by `CARRY_TURN_REFUSAL`.
- **`LatticeTurn` gains:**
  - `unapply`: the exact inverse (`m`'s transpose and Z's sign);
  - `then`: composition, where signed permutations compose into signed permutations.
- **Not yet wired:** nothing in `carry::Body` or the app uses it. That's steps B–D (B's design finding is posted on #637). So this PR is behaviour-neutral, new API plus tests.

## How tested

- **New `crates/sim/tests/field_carry.rs`, 3/3:**
  - `unapply_inverts_apply_and_then_composes`: all 8 turns over a 3-D sample lattice, and every ordered pair composes correctly.
  - `a_carried_field_reads_the_same_solid_through_every_turn`: a block with a slot cut through it (so the cut layer is live) reads **bit-identical** (`to_bits`) distance, mesh distance and parity at T(p) versus p, for all 8 turns.
  - `carrying_twice_is_carrying_through_the_composed_turn`
- **`scripts/gate.sh quick`:** the sim suites pass. Named: stock_backend_parity 13, stock_columns 3, and app setup_carry 9, carried_verify 8, rest_across_setups 7.
- **Clippy** on sim and app with `-D warnings`: clean. No golden changed.

## Not exercised

Steps B–E (the floor read, clipping, the body enum with its agreement lane, and the app holders), per #637.

Refs #637

title: Viewport origin gizmos wear their names (#641)
body:
With several setups on screen, every origin triad looks alike - nothing in the viewport says whose zero is whose (#641).

## The change

Every origin gizmo now labels itself at its origin. Each work-offset triad draws the entity name the Setup pane already uses (`G54` for the first setup, `Setup2/WCS` for the second) in bright triad blue at the ordinary overlay-label size; the dimmed world axes draw `World` in neutral gray dimmed by `WORLD_DIM`, like the lines under them. `Gizmo` (`interact.rs`) grows one `name` field, filled in `gizmos()` - which already honors the Models pane's eye (`hidden_offsets`) and the `show_world_axes` gate, so a hidden offset loses its name with its lines for free. `overlay_labels` places each name just below the projected origin (`NAME_DROP_UV = 0.02`, same currency as `axis_note::NOTE_DROP_UV`), emitted before the gizmo's `X`/`Y`/`Z` tips. Only the letters keep the big `is_axis_label` font. Rationale in `docs/decisions/641-viewport-gizmo-labels.md`.

## Pins (red on main, green with the fix)

- `gizmo_tests::the_dimmed_world_axes_are_labelled_world` - the fresh world's set carries `World`, neutral gray (equal channels) and dimmed like the axes.
- `gizmo_tests::each_triad_is_labelled_with_its_own_offset_name` - two setups: both `G54` and `Setup2/WCS` label their own origins, bright against the letters.
- `gizmo_tests::an_offset_name_stands_at_its_origin_not_its_axis_tips` - the name rides the projected origin horizontally, a small uv drop below it, not crowded onto the tips.
- `gizmo_tests::a_hidden_work_offset_drops_its_name_with_its_gizmo` - the pane's eye and the label agree.
- `gizmo_tests::gizmo_names_are_not_the_big_axis_letters` - `is_axis_label` still answers only X/Y/Z.
- Re-pins: label counts 3→4 (fresh world), 6→8 (two gizmos), 3→4 (moved origin); `axis_note_tests`' fresh-world set pins exactly `["World", "X", "Y", "Z"]`, which fixes each gizmo's emission order name-first.
- `setup_chip_tests`' no-G54-on-Setup2's-op clause narrows to plane chips (`" · "`): the `G54` origin name is Setup1's own, legitimately - the law was about op chips, and it still holds there.

## Tested

- Red first: with only the pins committed, `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- gizmo_tests axis_note_tests` ran 8 failed / 7 passed, exactly the new and re-pinned label tests - e.g. the fresh world's labels were `["X", "Y", "Z"]` with no name.
- Green: `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- gizmo_tests axis_note_tests setup_chip_tests` - 17 passed, 0 failed.
- Full lib: `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` - 382 passed, 0 failed (5 ignored). An earlier run of the same command failed only on `structural::shell_structure_light`, a theme-sync test this change never touches; it passes in isolation and on re-run - pre-existing parallel global-theme-state flakiness, already noted on #638.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --no-run` builds clean (untouched crate).
- Not exercised: the on-screen labels themselves - the producers are pinned instead.

Changelog: viewport origin gizmos now wear their names - each work-offset triad shows its Setup-pane name at its origin, the neutral world axes show World (#641)

Fixes #641

title: fix(turning): grooving and parting blades post their touched-off corner
body:
**Stacked on #640** (#630, tool orientation and the shared CL → control-point conversion). Review only this PR's own commit, `22658499`.

**P1 (#641):** grooving and parting posted the **middle of the blade's tip edge**, but a blade is touched off on a **corner**. With a left-corner touch-off, a groove landed w/2 off in Z and a part-off left the part w/2 short.
- **Verified on the kernels:** `blade.rs` plunges at band centres; `parting.rs` plunges at the parting plane, with the kerf at ±w/2.
- **Verified on the old golden:** a 3.2 groove from Z-3.6 to Z-6.8 cut with a 2 mm blade posted Z-4.6 and Z-5.8.

## What changed
- **Blades reuse #630's `orientation`,** read on the LinuxCNC chart. There is no new field or file key, and the same editor row and undoable `ChangeTool` apply.
  - **1**: the right corner (+Z).
  - **2**: the left corner (−Z). This is the **default**, from LinuxCNC Lathe User Information §4.2's parting example, a blade touched off on its left side.
  - **6**: the width centre, the old behaviour. **9** is read as 6.
- **Conversion:** `posting_nose.rs` shifts GrooveRough, GrooveFinish and Part paths by (0, ±w/2) through #640's rigid `control_point_path`.
  - X does not move: the CL radius is already the tip line.
  - There is no corner-radius term: a rounded corner's imaginary tip is the sharp corner.
- **Refused by name:** codes 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8 (ID or face), and a blade with no usable width.
- **Unchanged:** the cache, verifier, stock sim and gouge laws keep the true blade. The parting plane still means the kerf centre.
- **Editor:** a Groove tool's row reads "Touched-off corner" and offers only 1, 2 and 6. The tool note prints `ORIENTATION q`.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/641-blade-corner.md`.

**Behaviour change for existing programs:** the left-corner default moves every grooving and parting program by −w/2 in Z. A shop that touched off on the width centre sets its blades to 6.

## Golden diff (`fanuc-lathe/groove_part.nc`)
- **2 mm groove:** Z-5.8/-4.6 → **Z-6.8/-5.6**, the left corners at the walls.
- **3 mm part-off:** Z-10 → **Z-11.5**.
- Clearances move by the same amount; X is unchanged.

## How tested
- **New `lathe_blade_corner` (4 tests, each fails before the fix):**
  - a 3 mm groove at Z-10 posts Z-11.5, Z-8.5 or Z-10 for orientation 2, 1 or 6, and the cache stays at Z-10;
  - a part-off at Z-20 leaves the part's back face at Z-18.5 for every setting (before the fix, a left-corner blade left 17 mm);
  - ID and face codes are refused by name;
  - undo and redo.
- **Units and round-trip:** a tools unit for the blade chart, and `project_roundtrip::a_blade_corner_round_trips_and_old_blades_take_the_left_corner`.
- **Regressions, all green:** lathe_nose_tip, lathe_post, lathe_post_g76, lathe_post_refusals, lathe_field_sim, lathe_field_tools, turning, turning_blade, conformance, golden_cl, posting, project_roundtrip, commands_undo, the tool suites, tools lib, and the ui orientation row. Clippy is clean.

**Not exercised:** a Hub run, which comes with the lathe kit after #626.

Changelog: Grooving and parting blades post their touched-off corner (lathe orientation 1 = right, 2 = left (default), 6 = width centre) instead of the blade's width centre; ID/face codes are refused by name (#641)

Fixes #641

title: fix(app): a lathe thread's spindle arcs are judged by radius in the travel check
body:
## What changed

#631: the built-in Lathe (`lathe.mch`, X 0..320) refused **every thread**, with "move 2 reaches -5.600 in X, the stroke is 0.000..320.000".

**Cause:** a thread pass is a chain of arcs **about the spindle axis**. Their far side, and the travel check's added quarter points, read negative X. That's the CL's antipode: the spindle turning the work, never a slide position. The machine check judged that raw signed X.

**Fix** (`crates/app/src/machine/mod.rs`, the travel law in `check_ops`): on a machine of kind lathe, an XY arc **centred on the spindle axis** is judged in X by its **radius** at each extreme. Every other move keeps its signed X, so a real past-centre move is still judged against the band.

**Not changed:** the band itself. `lathe_stroke::lathe_x_stays_a_centreline_band` records that a lathe's X is a one-sided centreline band. Whether a nose-radius face to centre (#630 / PR #640, which ends at X -r) should widen it is #640's call, not this PR's.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/631-lathe-spindle-arc-travel.md`.

## How tested

- **New `crates/app/tests/lathe_thread_travel.rs`, 2/2:**
  - `a_thread_passes_the_built_in_lathe`: **fails without the fix**, with the issue's exact message ("move 2 reaches -5.600 in X…").
  - `a_real_over_travel_on_a_lathe_is_still_refused`: the same thread against an X stroke of 0..2 mm is refused "… in X".
- **`scripts/gate.sh quick`:** the app suites pass.
- **Named:**

  | Suite | Passed |
  |---|---|
  | machine | 32 |
  | machine_library | 11 |
  | turning_thread | 8 |
  | lathe_post | 7 |
  | lathe_post_g76 | 5 |
  | lathe_post_refusals | 5 |
  | tormach_machines | 5 |
  | conformance | 6 |
  | posting | 17 |
  | setup_mounts_post | 5 |
  | lathe_stroke | 5 |

- **`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings`:** clean, after the follow-up commit.
- No golden changed. Fork synced at v0.16.0.

## Not exercised

A Hub run on a lathe. The PathPilot lathe post is #626.

Changelog: A thread no longer fails the built-in Lathe's machine check - an arc about the spindle axis is judged by its radius, not its far side's negative X (#631)

Fixes #631

title: refactor(app): the operation priors and carried bounds read the stock through Columns
body:
## What changed

**Stacked on #595** (issue #585, the `Columns` seam). Merge #595 first. This is M7.3 step 3/6 (#26), **in part**.

The app's stock **readers** now read through the `Columns` seam instead of indexing a `Dexel` directly:

| Reader | Where |
|---|---|
| `prior_top` | `operation/top_stock.rs`: the prior top over a region |
| `revolved_surface` | `operation/drill_prior.rs`: a lathe axial hole's revolved prior |
| `columns_reach` | `operation/carried_stock.rs`: carried columns over a footprint |
| `carried_body_bounds` | `rest/across.rs`: the carried body's bounds |

They use the same lattice formulas (`Columns::cell`/`origin`/`center`/`col`/`top_at`), so **the answers are unchanged**. Callers wrap their grid with `Columns::of_grid`.

**Not in this PR: the holders.** Every app stock holder is either a plain grid or the **carried `Body`** (sim `carry.rs`). That's a two-sided column store with lattice flips and mirrors, which the app mutates directly (`simulate(&mut body.dex, ..)`, `lower`). Moving it onto `Stock` is a data-model design, not a seam move, so it's filed as **#637** with its open questions. #586 closes when #637 lands, so this PR is `Refs`.

## How tested

- **`scripts/gate.sh quick`:** the sim and app suites pass, **1850 passed, 0 failed**.

title: fix(turning): lathe posts write the tool's control point for its orientation, not the nose centre
body:
**P0 (#630):** lathe posts wrote the insert's **nose-centre** path under G40. With normal touch-off, the controlled point is the imaginary tip (LinuxCNC Lathe User Information §7.1), so turned diameters came out **2r oversize** and faces **r long**. Confirmed against the control vendor's own behaviour: PathPilot's conversational posts the orientation's control point with G40, and refuses a tool whose orientation can't make the cut. That sample is used as behaviour reference only.

## What changed
- **Tool orientation** (LinuxCNC 1-9 chart: Lathe User Information §3 figure, §7.1, §4.1):
  - `Tool.orientation: Option<u8>`. Turning inserts default to **2** (OD, cutting toward the chuck), boring bars to **3**.
  - Editable in the tool editor, which shows the default, through the undoable `ChangeTool`.
  - The project key is written only when set, so old files load with the default. 1-9 is enforced at command creation and at file read.
  - Fanuc's tip chart is different, and no post writes either number, so only the LinuxCNC chart is modelled.
- **One shared conversion,** `crates/post/src/post/nose_tip.rs::control_point_path`, called once from `posting::op_streams` (`posting_nose.rs`), not per .cps:
  - Every move, rapids and arc centres included, shifts by r·(ox, oz) for the orientation.
  - This is exact on diameters, faces, tapers and arcs: the cutting path is already the profile offset by r, and the insert is rigid.
  - Refused by name: a path on two meridians or off every meridian, a C angle, an off-plane arc, and paths carrying cycle, thread, compensation or probe records.
  - Converted ops: facing, profile rough/finish, chamfer, taper, multi-pass, boring. Grooving, parting, threading, form and drilling post as before.
- **The cache stays the nose centre.** The verifier, stock sim, gouge laws and CL goldens are unchanged. Orientation is not part of the op stamp, so editing it never stales an op.
- **Orientation fit, refused by name at post:** a corner tip reaches within 45° of its direction, an axis tip within 90°, and 9 fits anything.
  - Facing needs −Z and −X (2, 6, 7 fit), OD turning −X, boring +X.
  - A cut needing −X and +Z gives exactly [1, 5, 6], matching PathPilot's own refusal.
- **fanuc-lathe.cps:** the header states the control-point rule (G40). The tool note adds `ORIENTATION q` from a new commentary parameter `PARAM ToolOrientation`, documented in CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/630-nose-tip.md`.

## Golden diffs (Fanuc Lathe; r = 0.8, orientation 2)
- **`facing.nc`:** every changed line shifts X −1.6 (diameter) and Z −0.8. The last pass now posts the facing plane (Z14, was Z14.8).
  - Passes end at **X-1.6**: the nose centre still reaches the axis, so the control point stands r past centre. This is a normal facing overtravel, but a machine with a 0 X limit would need #631.
- **`profile_rough_finish.nc`:** shifts by X −1.6 / Z −0.8. The Ø12 flange posts **X12** (was X13.6), the shoulder Z2 (was Z2.8), and the Ø7 neck X7 (was X8.6). Three points differ by 0.001 from a pure shift because of 1 µm grid rounding.
- **Unchanged:** groove/part, axial drill, thread G76 and C-axis goldens. In `lathe_post.rs`, the facing assertion now expects `X-1.6 Z14` and `ORIENTATION 2`.

## How tested
- **`nose_tip` units (7):**
  - the OD finish posts the finished diameter, and a face posts Z0;
  - every orientation's offset;
  - a 30° taper is exact;
  - arcs keep their radius and move their centre;
  - the X-meridian case;
  - refusals;
  - orientation 9 is identity.
- **`orientation` units (3),** including PathPilot's [1, 5, 6].
- **App `lathe_nose_tip` (6):**
  - a Ø19.05 neck posts X19.05 and the shoulder Z0, while the cache stays nose-centre;
  - facing reaches the axis;
  - every fitting orientation equals cache + r·offset, and editing never stales the op;
  - mismatched orientations are refused;
  - ChangeTool undo/redo, and code 10 is refused;
  - a boring bar defaults to 3.
- **Round-trip and UI:** `project_roundtrip::a_lathe_orientation_round_trips_and_old_tools_take_the_default`, and the UI orientation row.
- **Gate:**
  - the non-thread turning and lathe suites, `lathe_post_g76`, conformance, golden_cl, posting, project_roundtrip and commands_undo;
  - the tool suites, c_axis_live, control_comp, wear_comp, program_entry, inverted_post and coolant_followups;
  - camcraft-post and camcraft-tools.
  - Clippy is clean on 5 crates.

## Follow-ups
- **Grooving and parting blades:** they post the centre of the blade's width, but a blade is touched off on a corner (LinuxCNC §4.2), so a width/2 Z offset is likely owed. Filed separately.
- **Refusal rule:** checking the leading direction would need insert lead angles, which the tool library doesn't model.
- **#626 (PathPilot lathe post):** consumes the converted stream once merged; its goldens need regenerating.
- **#639 (#629):** may hit small conflicts in test `Tool` literals.

Changelog: Lathe posts write the turning tool's control point for its orientation (LinuxCNC 1-9, editable per tool; default 2 for turning inserts, 3 for boring bars) instead of the nose-centre path: a Ø19.05 finish now posts X19.05 and a face at Z0 posts Z0; an orientation that cannot cut the operation is refused by name (#630)

title: fix(turning): threads cut right-hand toward the chuck by default; the hand is stated, never dropped
body:
**P0 (#629):** every lathe thread was cut **left-hand**. The engine ran every pass toward +Z (away from the chuck), and the Fanuc Lathe post wrote `M03` and dropped the CL's arc sense. Confirmed against the control vendor's own behaviour: PathPilot Hub 8L conversational right-hand OD G76 runs toward −Z under M3. That sample is cited as behaviour confirmation only.

## What changed
- **Hand rule:** `cl::ThreadHand` (Right by default, or Left). A helix is RH if it turns ccw (seen from +Z) while rising, or cw while falling. With the free end at +Z, M03 means the tool goes cw around the part, so a cw half-turn needs M03 and a ccw one M04.
- **Engine (`turning/thread.rs`):** every pass starts at the top and **descends toward the chuck**. Arc sense = `hand.ccw_for(true)`, and the infeed schedule is unchanged.
- **Record and stream:**
  - `ThreadCycle.hand`; `is_sane` requires every half-turn to wind that hand.
  - The `THREAD … HAND right|left` word is required.
  - `PARAM SpindleDirection "reverse"` is emitted when M04 is needed.
  - New manifest flag `threadHands`: a script without it is refused a reverse section by name. Documented in CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md and assets/posts/AGENTS.md.
- **fanuc-lathe.cps:**
  - writes M03, or M04 (with an operator note) when the stream asks for reverse;
  - checks **every G32 half-turn** against the spindle it wrote and refuses a mismatch ("would cut the other hand");
  - G76 refuses a record with no hand, or one whose hand and Z direction need the other spindle.
- **Verdict:** `thread_hand_warnings` raises a Gouge at the first wrong-hand half-turn, so the gate blocks.
- **App:**
  - `OpParams::Threading { hand }` (Right).
  - The project file always writes `hand`; an old file loads as Right.
  - The cache stamp includes the hand, so every old threading cache goes Stale once and regenerates toward the chuck.
  - MCP picks it up through the params DTO.
  - UI: a "Hand" row on the Passes tab, undoable.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/629-thread-hand.md` (no project version bump: reasoning inside; the feed-away-from-chuck option is left for a follow-up).

**Golden diff** (`fanuc-lathe/thread_g76.nc`): `G00 X12.1 Z8` → `Z14`, and `G76 X9.6 Z14 …` → `Z8 …`. The cycle now starts at the top and feeds toward the chuck under M03.

## How tested
- **New tests (each fails on the old code):**
  - motion: `every_pass_runs_toward_the_chuck_and_the_helix_winds_the_asked_hand` and `the_hand_of_a_turn_is_the_screw_law`;
  - app `lathe_post_g76`: `a_right_hand_thread_posts_toward_the_chuck_under_m03` (18 G32 blocks descending, G76 Z14→Z8), `a_left_hand_thread_posts_toward_the_chuck_under_m04` and `the_hand_is_never_dropped`;
  - `lathe_post_refusals`: ccw falling under M03 is refused;
  - `turning_thread`: hand edit undo/redo;
  - `project_roundtrip`: an old file loads as Right, Left survives, and an invalid word is refused;
  - ui: the hand row.
- **Gate:** motion, post, cl and the app lathe, turning, inverted, conformance, golden_cl, posting, project_roundtrip, commands_undo and mcp suites pass. Clippy is clean on 5 crates.

## Follow-ups and merge notes
- **#626 (PathPilot lathe post):** must declare `threadHands`, read `PARAM SpindleDirection`, check half-turn sense, and take the G76 direction from Z→EndZ.
- **Threading stack (#516-#518, #468):** must carry `hand` and keep the descending passes and arc sense.

Changelog: Lathe threads cut right-hand toward the chuck under M03 by default; Threading gains a Hand (Right/Left, LH posts M04), the thread record and stream state the hand, and the Fanuc Lathe post refuses any pass or G76 whose hand disagrees with its spindle (#629)

Fixes #629

title: fix(#622): view-cube pole clicks keep the roll, snapped to the nearest quarter turn
body:
Clicking TOP/BOT on the view cube threw the roll away. A face click commands `Camera::toward(face normal)`; at a Z pole the normalized direction is exactly `[0, 0, +-1]`, so `toward` read `yaw = atan2(0, 0) = 0` and `basis_right`'s zero-guard returned literal world `+X` whatever the yaw - every pole click landed on one canonical orientation and the model spun up to 180 degrees on screen (#622 repro: orbit near-overhead at yaw ~90 deg, click TOP, the part rotates half a turn).

## The change

`Camera::toward` (`viewport.rs`) grows one clause: when the normalized direction is exactly a Z pole (`n[2].abs() == 1.0`), the yaw is the *pre-click* camera's yaw snapped to the nearest quarter turn, `(yaw / FRAC_PI_2).round() * FRAC_PI_2`, instead of the vanishing atan2. `basis_right`'s pole guard evaluates that yaw - `(-yaw.sin(), yaw.cos(), 0.0)` - which is the same expression the guard already produces for every non-pole view, extended to the one point where `cross(forward, +Z)` underflows `normalize`'s EPSILON floor (`cos(pi/2)^2 ~ 3.7e-33`).

Result: a near-pole click turns the screen frame at most 45 degrees from the up it had (the snap's own bound); screen up/right still ride world axes at the pole (the surviving half of the old law); views sharing a quarter turn roll alike; and a second click at the same pole is exact idempotence - the reported double-click twitch cannot happen. Non-pole directions (edges, corners, `oriented`, orbit) are untouched. Rationale in `docs/decisions/622-viewcube-roll-snap.md`.

## Pins (red on main, green with the fix)

- `law_tests::view_cube_tests::pole_views_hold_a_stable_roll` - re-pinned from "screen right is +X at both poles for arbitrary yaws" to the quarter-turn law: right `(-sin y_s, cos y_s, 0)`, up `(-cos y_s, -sin y_s, 0)` at TOP / `(cos y_s, sin y_s, 0)` at BOT.
- `law_tests::view_cube_tests::toward_turns_the_eye_without_moving_it` - new cases: start yaw 2.0 -> TOP lands `pi/2`; start yaw -2.3 -> BOT lands `-pi/2`.
- `law_tests::view_cube_tests::a_pole_click_keeps_the_roll_the_view_had` - near-pole view (yaw 1.0, pitch 1.5), TOP click lands the on-screen up within 45 degrees of the pre-click up. On main the swing is ~147 degrees.
- `law_tests::view_cube_tests::a_second_pole_click_lands_the_same_view` - the reported double-click: the second `toward([0,0,1])` changes nothing (passes before and after; it pins the property the issue asked for).

## Tested

- Red first: with only the pins committed, `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib view_cube_tests` runs 3 failed / 4 passed, exactly the predicted law breaks - `a pole click keeps the pre-click yaw's quarter turn: 0` (`[-0.5389488413540798, -0.8393630887186533, 0.07073720166770292] -> [-0.0, 1.0, 0.0]`), and `screen right at the [0.0, 0.0, 1.0] pole: [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]`.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --no-run` builds clean.
- Green: `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib view_cube_tests` - 7 passed, 0 failed.
- Full lib: `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` - 379 passed, 0 failed (5 ignored). One earlier run failed only on `structural::shell_structure_light`, a theme-sync test this change never touches; it passes in isolation and on re-run - pre-existing parallel global-theme-state flakiness.
- The `egui_app` view-cube gesture tests (face click orients, arms nothing) pass untouched.
- Not exercised: the full app suite beyond the two crates, and the on-screen cube itself - the law is pinned instead.

Changelog: view-cube TOP/BOT clicks now land the pole view at the nearest quarter-turn roll instead of spinning the model to canonical +X (#622)

Fixes #622

title: perf(sim): a field block stock builds in closed form, not by band fill
body:
## What changed

#633: the field stock engine was about 300× slower than the column engine on a large box (found in PR #625's review). This blocked #589, the column engine's retirement.

**Profile** (release, `drill_plate.cl` on a 120 mm box at the CLI's 0.375 mm auto cell, 320 × 320):

| Phase | Column | Field, before | **Field, after** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Build the block | 27 µs | **58 s** | **42 µs** |
| Cut (9 moves) | 23 µs | 3.4 ms | 2.6 ms |
| Read every column | 0.2 ms | 66 ms | 53 ms |
| Cut cells | 399 | 399 | **399** |

- **Cause:** it was not the cutting (the M7.3 per-brick law, #584, holds). `block_field` meshes the floorless block **ten spans deep**, and `SdfField::from_mesh`'s BFS band-filled every cell along those 1.2 m walls.
- **Fix:** a new `field_box::AnalyticBox`, the closed-form signed distance of an axis-aligned box.
  - `SdfField::from_box` builds the block's shell, which is a handful of facets and still answers parity and bounds, and **stores no bricks**.
  - `mag_at`, the single reader of the mesh layer, answers unstored cells from the box, clamped to `cap` by the existing band law.
  - The cut layers and every other reader are unchanged. Cylinder and model stocks still band-fill, bounded by their real size.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/633-field-block-closed-form.md`.

## How tested

- **New `crates/sim/tests/field_block_cost.rs`, 3/3:**
  - `a_block_stores_no_band_at_build`: the 58 s case stores 0 bricks.
  - `the_closed_form_reads_the_stock_the_band_fill_read`: across a lattice around a block, same sign everywhere and agreement within 2 cells with the band-filled field.
  - `a_large_field_block_runs_a_drill_program_quickly`: heavy lane, release, a 120 mm block plus 4 plunges under 2 s.
- **Heavy release lanes**, run to confirm verdicts are unchanged:
  - `stock_engine_agreement`: 3/3, **0 findings**, every `max |delta|` 0.
  - `stock_backend_parity`: 13/13.
  - `stock_field_cost`: total **7.6 s (was 83.9 s)**. Build is 0.00 s on every golden program, at 0.19-10.9 ms/move.
- **`scripts/gate.sh quick`:** the sim suites pass. Named: stock_columns 3, stock_preview 10, stock_bull_nose 7, wall_slack 5, headless_bin 3, and app stock_sim_document 9, stock_view 4, stock_play 7, setup_carry 9, carried_verify 8.
- **Clippy** on sim and app with `-D warnings`: clean. No golden changed.

## Not exercised

Cylinder and model-stock build cost. Those still band-fill; a closed-form cylinder can follow if profiling shows a need.

Changelog: The field stock engine builds a block stock in microseconds instead of up to a minute (closed-form box distance) (#633)

Fixes #633

title: feat(post): per-operation smoothing, opt-in, in every mill dialect
body:
## What changed

Requested by @spikeypineapple on #616. Smoothing differs per control, and the "auto" behaviour is maximum accuracy on finishing, with roughing aggressiveness following the stock left. The design was posted on the issue before code.

- **The option:** **"Smoothing per operation"**, a new document post option (`PostOptions.smoothing`), **off by default**.
  - **Off:** no smoothing PARAM is in the stream, so every program, and the `postOptions` object, is **byte-identical**.
  - **Saving:** the additive `smoothing` project key, absent when off. Undoable through `SetPostOptions`, and offered as a checkbox under the post picker for every mill post.
- **On, each operation states its ask** (`app::smoothing::of`) as `PARAM Smoothing <mm>` + `PARAM SmoothingMode finish|rough`:
  - **finish:** an op with a contour tolerance and no stock left asks **half** its tolerance (the control's deviation stacks on the verified path);
  - **rough:** an op leaving stock asks **stock × 0.2, capped at 0.25 mm, never more than that fifth** (no floor);
  - **nothing:** drilling, tapping, probing, threading, facing and the lathe kinds ask nothing.
- **Each mill post writes its control's words** after the section preamble and **undoes them at the section end**, so no tolerance leaks:

  | Post | On | Off |
  |---|---|---|
  | Tormach / LinuxCNC | `G64 P<tol>` | the header's `G64 P0.001` / `P0.025` |
  | Fanuc | one note "SMOOTHING NOT WRITTEN - G5.1 STATES NO TOLERANCE" (G5.1 has no tolerance word; review of #635) | none |
  | Haas | `G187 P3\|P1 E<tol>` | `G187` |
  | Siemens 840D | `CYCLE832(<tol>,_FINISH\|_ROUGH,1)` | `CYCLE832()` |
  | Heidenhain (ISO) | `G62 T<tol>` | `G62` |
  | Mazak | one note "SMOOTHING NOT WRITTEN - NO MAZAK FORM STATED" (no guessed word) | none |

- **Fanuc writes nothing yet:** `G5.1 Q1` states no tolerance, so it can't be held to the op's ask. A bounded form can follow with #614's Doosan sample. Decision record: `docs/decisions/616-smoothing.md`.

## How tested

- **New `crates/app/tests/smoothing.rs`, 4/4:**
  - `off_is_byte_identical_and_writes_no_smoothing_word`: every mill post.
  - `each_dialect_writes_its_words_and_undoes_them_at_the_section_end`: finish and rough per dialect; the words are stated before the first cut and reset after.
  - `mazak_names_the_ask_once_and_writes_no_guessed_word`
  - `finish_ops_ask_their_tolerance_and_rough_ops_ask_from_their_stock`: including the clamp ends and drill → none.
- **`scripts/gate.sh quick`:** post and app suites pass after the follow-up commit. The first run caught `lathe_post_g76` pinning the whole `postOptions` object; the key is now omitted when off. The only ui reds are the 3 known GPU-adapter tests (#615 / #623).
- **Named, all with the option off:**

  | Suite | Passed |
  |---|---|
  | conformance | 6 |
  | golden_cl | 23 |
  | posting | 17 |
  | tormach_post | 10 |
  | fanuc_post | 11 |
  | heidenhain_block_form | 4 |
  | sinumerik_safe_retract | 3 |
  | coolant | 7 |
  | after_op | 10 |
  | project_roundtrip | 69 |
  | per_op_files | 9 |
  | lathe_post_g76 | 5 |
  | ui structural / post_options / after_op | 5 |

- **Clippy** on post, app and ui with `-D warnings`: clean. **No golden or snapshot changed.**

## Not exercised

A run on a real control or simulator with smoothing on. PathPilot Hub can check the Tormach `G64 P` per section. The Haas `G187`, Siemens `CYCLE832` and Heidenhain `G62` words come from public documentation and haven't been run on a control. That's why the option is opt-in.

Changelog: An opt-in "Smoothing per operation" post option writes each control's smoothing mode per operation (finish tolerance or a roughing deviation from the stock left): G64 P, G5.1, G187, CYCLE832, G62 (#616)

Fixes #616

title: fix(ui): GPU tests fall back to the hardware adapter and say when they skip
body:
## What changed
Every GPU test, and the real `--headless` run, requested `force_fallback_adapter: true`, a software adapter. Metal has none. So on every Mac:
- `gpu_render`, `trace_composite` and `trace_parity` silently skipped and reported **pass**;
- `headless_run_succeeds` and the two headless CLI tests **failed** with "No suitable graphics adapter found".

New `crates/ui/src/headless_gpu.rs`:
- **`device()`:** tries the software adapter first (deterministic CI on Linux/Windows), then the default hardware adapter. It returns the device, queue, which kind it got and the adapter's name and backend. If both fail, the error names both reasons.
- **`device_for_test(suite)`:** prints the adapter it renders on. With no adapter it prints a loud `*** <suite>: SKIPPED (no adapter) - NOT a pass ***`, and `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1` turns that into a failure.
- **Headless app path:** `headless::run` (shell.rs) now uses the helper, so the CLI tests are fixed through the app path itself.
- **Not an `#[ignore]` lane:** that would drop these ~1 s suites from quick and batch everywhere. Reasoning in `docs/decisions/615-gpu-adapter.md`.

## How tested (on a real Apple M3 Max, Metal)
| Suite | Before | After |
|---|---|---|

title: feat(mcp): an idle live-session client is dropped after a timeout
body:
**Stacked on #474** (#183, MCP live in the GUI). It includes #474's commits until that PR merges.

## What changed
The live listener (`crates/app/src/mcp/listen.rs`) serves one client at a time, and a silent local connection held the session until it hung up.
- **Idle window:** a new `IDLE_TIMEOUT` of 5 minutes. A client that sends no complete line for that long gets one `notifications/message` warning and is disconnected. The log names it (`client <peer> dropped: idle - …; serving the next client`), and the next client is served.
- **What counts as idle:** the clock restarts after each answered line. Time spent answering doesn't count, and a partial line doesn't reset it. Windows shorter than the 50 ms poll step are raised to it.
- **Constructor:** `Inbox::listen_with_idle(port, wake, idle)` is new. `Inbox::listen` uses the default, so the GUI caller is unchanged.
- **Kept from #474:** the JSON-lines-only rule, the `MAX_LINE` read cap, the 5 s write timeout and stop/join on drop.
- **Not done:** a new client replacing an idle one, because it would let any local process kick a live agent off between calls. The reasoning is in `docs/decisions/567-mcp-idle-timeout.md`.

## How tested
- `mcp_live::an_idle_client_is_dropped_by_name_and_the_next_one_is_served` (300 ms window): a silent client gets the note and then EOF, not early, and the log names it. A second client is served afterwards.
- `mcp_live::a_client_that_keeps_talking_is_never_dropped_as_idle`: eight pings 150 ms apart, all answered.
- **Before the change:** the idle test fails with the window forced back to 5 minutes.
- **Gate:** app `mcp_live` 9 and ui `mcp_live` 2 pass; clippy (app and ui, `-D warnings`) is clean.

Changelog: The live MCP listener drops a client that sends nothing for 5 minutes, telling it why and logging its address, so the next agent can connect (#567)

Fixes #567

title: feat(post): probing hooks for the Haas, Mazak and Siemens posts
body:
**Replaces #360** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

## What changed
- **`haas.cps`: probes.** It adds `onProbeMove` / `onProbeRetreat` / `onProbeResult`:
  - G31 skip; #5061–#5063 trip read; no-contact and out-of-tolerance alarms through `#3000`;
  - incremental G91 back-off;
  - `G10 L2 P` from `#5221+20×slot`, or a `#3006` operator stop.
  - Source: the Haas Mill Operator's Manual (public).
- **`mazak.cps`: probes.** The same macro-B contract in Mazak EIA/ISO words:
  - `IF[..]GOTO` with unique N labels, since `IF..THEN` is not documented on every EIA generation;
  - the operator stop is a comment plus M00.
  - Source: Mazak's EIA/ISO programming manual (Fanuc-compatible).
- **`sinumerik.cps`: probes.**
  - `MEAS=1 G1`; `$AC_MEA[1]` checks for no contact; `$AA_MW[..]` reads the trip into R50–R61.
  - `IF..ENDIF` + `MSG` + `SETAL` + `M0` alarms; incremental G91 back-off.
  - Sets the offset through `$P_UIFR[..,TR]` (FI copied when the frame changes), then re-selects the active G5x.
  - It refuses by name to set G58/G59 (axial offsets on an 840D) or to work from an offset outside G54–G57 / G505–G599.
  - Source: SINUMERIK 840D sl Programming Manual (Fundamentals / Job Planning).
- **`heidenhain.cps`: still refused by name.** The TNC 640 ISO manual this post follows documents no skip move and no trip-position variable; TNC probing lives in the separate touch-probe-cycles manual. The script now carries a comment saying so, and the existing engine refusal is pinned.
- **Spindle at 0 rpm.** Haas, Mazak and Siemens no longer write a spindle-on block at 0 rpm (a touch probe), as fanuc already did. No existing golden contained `S0`.
- **Protected positioning moves (#174's `onProbeGuard`).** Merged with main; every GUARD record (descent, travel, rise) is now written as a stop-on-contact move that alarms on an unexpected trip:
  - Haas: `G31` + `IF[ABS[#506x-target]GT0.001]THEN#3000=3(PROBE HIT ON POSITIONING)` per moving axis.
  - Mazak: the same test as `IF[..LE0.001]GOTOn` / `#3000=3(..)` / `Nn`.
  - Sinumerik: `MEAS=1 G1` + `IF $AC_MEA[1]==1` -> `MSG`, `SETAL(65002)`, `M0`, `ENDIF`.
  - Haas/Mazak fold a negative target's sign (`minusU`, as fanuc), so no `#5061--7`.
- `docs/decisions/173-probe-hooks-dialects.md` names every source and judgement call.

## How tested
- New `crates/app/tests/probe_dialects.rs` (13 tests, incl. `haas_guards_positioning_moves_with_a_hit_alarm`, `mazak_guards_positioning_moves_with_a_hit_alarm`, `sinumerik_guards_positioning_moves_with_a_hit_alarm`): bore-centre goldens `golden/nc/{haas,mazak,sinumerik}/probe_bore_centre.nc` (G55 set from G54), both operator-stop variants, the Sinumerik G59 refusal, and the Heidenhain refusal.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick` (macOS): post suites ok. App suites: everything passes except `probe_op::every_older_kind_keeps_its_stored_id_and_digest_tag`. That test pins `PROJECT_VERSION == 51`, but main is now at 53, so it fails the same way on `upstream/main`; PR #345 fixes it. This commit touches no Rust source.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --tests` is clean.

## Not exercised
- **No controller or simulator run yet**, so this stays a draft. The posted words follow the public manuals only.
  - Mazak is the weakest-sourced: its `#5061` / `#5221` numbering should be confirmed against a Mazak manual.
  - Sinumerik's MEAS/`$AA_MW` path needs a check on a real 840D or a simulator.
- **The probe is not armed by the post.** Arming is machine-specific and stated by no stream record. An unarmed probe never trips, so it raises the no-contact alarm, which matches fanuc.

Changelog: The Haas, Mazak and Siemens 840D posts write the Probe operation (skip move, trip read, tolerance alarm, set work offset); Heidenhain keeps a named refusal (#173)

Refs #173 (Heidenhain stays a named refusal)
